<subject>Cutoff Time for End-of-Day Gas Transactions</subject>
<body>
Dear all,

A couple of weeks ago, I spoke with each of you regarding this matter, but it was postponed due to other urgent priorities. Nevertheless, you all agreed that establishing a standard cutoff time for UK gas, power, and liquids transactions would be appropriate.

The optimal approach would be to set the cutoff at 4pm daily. To provide some context, I reviewed yesterday’s activity to see how many deals were executed after 4pm London time. There were three UK Gas trades and two European Gas trades. Post-4pm, any unsettled deals would automatically roll over to the next business day. However, for deals that do not roll over after 4pm, the respective risk teams will need to treat them as the following day’s transactions. I’m unsure how this might impact Risk’s procedures for traders’ position reporting, since official books would exclude these late trades. Would Risk be able to produce supplemental reports each morning to ensure desks have accurate positions?

Please share any feedback you may have, and in any case, kindly confirm whether a 4pm cutoff works for your teams.

Best regards,  
Alex  
Meridian Law & Advisory LLP  
x48219  

James – are there any potential issues with the daily position reconciliation?  
Claire – we touched on this briefly a few weeks ago; any additional thoughts?
</body>
